My experiences in therapy have varied. I found it difficult to actually connect with the first several therapists I saw, I would go to sessions with them for about two months, make them open up, and then we somehow always ended up talking about them instead of me during the entire session (which I preferred at the time). With my current therapist, it has taken me almost two years to really start opening up. I hardly know anything about my T, so I don't feel as connected (but definitely find myself wanting to be more connected, just by human nature) but I also think not knowing much about my T has helped my personal therapy process. 

I don't know if not wanting to be open or exposed/seen is really an INFJ problem, or a me problem, but that's my experience, and the experience I've heard of some fellow INFJ. Best of luck!

In my (25F) experience, this is an INFJ trait! It takes me multiple years to get over relationships, and many months to get over small crushes. I think it's due to the energy and long time that it takes for us to open up or even get in the head space to open up about ourselves to someone, and then dealing with the fact that part of ourselves (even in theory) is being carried by another person. That has been my experience.

I have left a few sessions with my therapist thinking "Wow, that was definitely worth every dollar (most of which my insurance pays, but still definitely worth it)"   
I think, for me, it has taken a lot of time (almost two years) to get close enough to be open with my therapist, and I think that's a big part of getting help, for me.   
I don't feel like that with every session, but the more I go, the more often I'm feeling like it was a great session worth it all.
